title: Canonical operator interface
specification: The system shall provide one browser-based Command Center as the primary interface for routine operator workflows.

title: State clarity
specification: The interface shall distinguish at minimum: unavailable, ready, queued, running, cancelling, completed, failed, cancelled, and not verified, where those states apply.

title: Action feedback
specification: For each consequential operator action, the system shall provide an outcome or a clear reason the action could not start.

title: Error guidance
specification: User-facing errors shall identify the failed operation, the known impact, and a safe next step when one is available.

title: Capability disclosure
specification: The system shall report the capabilities and prerequisites detected for the current environment without implying that detection alone proves end-to-end operation.

title: No competing primary UX
specification: Supporting CLI tools or scripts shall not introduce a separate, competing primary operator experience.

title: Declared support envelope
specification: The project shall define supported operating systems, runtime versions, hardware assumptions, and optional dependencies.

title: Preflight
specification: The system shall check required prerequisites before starting a workflow that depends on them and shall identify unmet prerequisites.

title: Clean installation
specification: Installation and launch shall be verifiable from a clean environment using documented instructions and no undeclared local state.

title: Archive distribution
specification: Where source ZIP download is presented as a supported acquisition method, the project shall test installation from that archive as well as from a clean Git clone.

title: Non-destructive self-test
specification: The system shall offer a self-test that does not modify user datasets or overwrite valuable artifacts.

title: Network disclosure
specification: Installation and runtime documentation shall identify required downloads, external services, and offline limitations.

title: Explicit workflow configuration
specification: Each supported workflow shall have a validated configuration with documented defaults and constraints.

title: Stage identity
specification: Each run and stage shall have stable identifiers that correlate status, logs, inputs, outputs, and failures.

title: Lifecycle semantics
specification: Runs shall expose defined states and valid transitions. Invalid transitions shall be rejected or handled explicitly.

title: Cancellation
specification: Cancellation behavior shall be defined for each long-running stage, including what is stopped, what state is preserved, and how partial output is marked.

title: Retry safety
specification: Retry behavior shall identify whether the operation is safe to repeat, resumes from a checkpoint, or requires a new run.

title: Bounded execution
specification: The system shall limit concurrent work and resource use according to explicit configuration and the supported hardware envelope.

title: Failure isolation
specification: A failed stage shall not be reported as successful, and downstream stages shall not consume incomplete outputs unless the workflow explicitly supports and validates partial results.

title: Job scheduling
specification: If multiple jobs are supported, queueing, ordering, concurrency, cancellation, and resource admission behavior shall be specified and tested. If they are not supported, the product shall enforce and communicate the actual single-job or bounded-execution policy.

title: Input identity
specification: Each run shall record sufficient identity for its inputs, such as path reference, content hash, dataset version, or a documented equivalent appropriate to the source.

title: Transformation lineage
specification: Supported data-preparation stages shall record configuration and outputs sufficient to reconstruct the declared processing lineage.

title: Critical persistence
specification: Critical state, manifests, and metadata shall be written atomically or through an equivalent mechanism that prevents readers from observing partially written records.

title: Validation before use
specification: Manifests and configuration shall be validated before downstream use, and malformed or inconsistent records shall fail clearly.

title: Immutable run evidence
specification: Once a run is finalized, its recorded configuration and provenance shall not be silently rewritten by later runs.

title: Checkpoint integrity
specification: Checkpoints shall be associated with run identity, step/epoch information where applicable, model/configuration identity, and integrity metadata where feasible.

title: Safe serialization
specification: Loading untrusted or externally supplied artifacts shall use safe formats and loading modes where available. Any less-safe compatibility path shall be explicitly justified, constrained, and documented.

title: Schema evolution
specification: Persistent records shall carry a schema version or equivalent migration marker when their structure is expected to evolve.

title: Supported combinations
specification: The system shall declare which model sizes, backends, precision modes, and configuration combinations are supported, experimental, or unsupported.

title: Resource preflight
specification: Before a resource-intensive run, the system shall estimate or report relevant CPU, RAM, VRAM, storage, and other measurable constraints, stating uncertainty and limitations.

title: No false guarantees
specification: Resource estimates shall not be presented as guarantees of successful completion.

title: Training evidence
specification: A completed training run shall record applicable configuration, software/backend versions, data identity, seed where relevant, progress, and metrics needed to interpret the result.

title: Evaluation context
specification: Metrics shall include definitions and enough evaluation context to prevent misleading comparisons.

title: Comparability
specification: Run comparison shall identify material differences in data, model, tokenizer, configuration, evaluation method, and environment. Non-comparable runs shall not be presented as directly equivalent.

title: Completion semantics
specification: A process exit code alone shall not establish that training or evaluation succeeded; output validation and required postconditions shall also be checked.

title: Resource stop conditions
specification: The system shall define safe behavior for cancellation, out-of-space conditions, process crashes, and configured resource limits.

title: Artifact identity
specification: Produced artifacts shall have stable identity and be linked to the run and configuration that produced them.

title: Export validation
specification: Each supported export format shall have a defined validation procedure that checks expected files, metadata, and format-specific integrity.

title: Dataset documentation
specification: Every model export shall be accompanied by a model-specific dataset card or equivalent dataset documentation that identifies the data used, processing lineage, known limitations, and relevant provenance. The export shall fail validation if this required documentation is absent.

title: Model documentation
specification: Export documentation shall identify model architecture/family, intended use, known limitations, training/evaluation context, and compatibility requirements to the extent known.

title: Paired integrity
specification: The model artifact and its required documentation shall be packaged and tracked as one logical export unit, with a manifest or integrity mechanism that detects missing or mismatched components.

title: Format-specific claims
specification: The system shall not claim compatibility with a runtime or format unless the export has been validated against the declared support contract.

title: Export lifecycle
specification: Copying, renaming, moving, or deleting artifacts shall preserve or deliberately update their provenance links; stale references shall be detectable.

title: Structured logs
specification: Logs shall include appropriate timestamps, severity, run/stage identifiers, and event context.

title: Redaction
specification: Logs and diagnostic bundles shall redact secrets and avoid unnecessary exposure of private data.

title: Diagnostic bundle
specification: The system should provide a user-triggered diagnostic bundle containing relevant configuration, versions, status, and logs, with a preview or disclosure of included data.

title: Health reporting
specification: Health/readiness checks shall distinguish application health from availability of optional capabilities and external dependencies.

title: Recovery guidance
specification: Known recoverable failures shall have documented recovery procedures, including what evidence or data may be lost.

title: Backup and restore
specification: Persistent user data that cannot be recreated without cost shall have a documented backup/restore strategy, including verification and failure handling.

title: Cleanup safety
specification: Cleanup operations shall preview affected paths and estimated impact before deleting user data, unless a separately approved non-interactive policy explicitly governs the operation.

title: Retention
specification: Log and artifact retention rules shall be explicit, bounded where appropriate, and configurable where user needs differ.

title: Least privilege
specification: The application shall request only permissions needed for documented functionality.

title: Path safety
specification: File operations shall validate paths and prevent unintended traversal outside approved roots.

title: Secret handling
specification: Credentials and secrets shall not be embedded in source, committed configuration, or ordinary logs.

title: Dependency integrity
specification: Dependencies and packaged executables shall be versioned and checked using appropriate lockfiles, hashes, signatures, or provenance evidence where feasible.

title: Explicit external effects
specification: Network transfers, external-service calls, and destructive operations shall be disclosed and bounded.

title: Threat review
specification: Features that execute external binaries, load model artifacts, process untrusted data, or delete files shall receive a documented security review.

title: Layered tests
specification: The project shall maintain unit, integration, end-to-end, and packaging/installation tests appropriate to each capability.

title: Failure-path testing
specification: Tests shall cover expected failures such as subprocess launch failure, nonzero exit, interrupted writes, invalid configuration, missing prerequisites, cancellation, and partial artifacts.

title: Environment matrix
specification: Mandatory workflows shall be tested across the approved support matrix, including relevant CPU/GPU and constrained-resource scenarios.

title: Clean-machine evidence
specification: Release candidates shall be installed and exercised in a clean environment with no undeclared local dependencies or cached build artifacts.

title: Revision/package identity
specification: Release evidence shall identify the exact source revision, build inputs, package, and relevant dependency versions.

title: Honest release gate
specification: Any mandatory criterion marked failed, blocked, or not tested shall prevent a release from being described as fully certified.

title: Evidence retention
specification: Test reports and release evidence shall be retained in a form that can be reviewed and tied to the candidate.
